correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 all conditional events are positive. Forest-count and derangement factors produce an exact conditional law. A cycle-indicator argument proves the mean. Strict monotonicity of the finite positive sum S_m proves strict convexity; exact telescoping at m=n-1,n proves unique minimum k=1 and the birthday-scale gap. Two tail thresholds use D_1=0 and yield opposite strict signs for all 1<=k<=n-2. A separate vertexwise conditioning and telescoping argument proves Cov(K,C)=0. The finite exact checker is corroboration, not an infinite proof; the Gaussian asymptotic follows via controlled product estimates and Riemann sum.

value.rationale: Fixed points are a natural directly observable feature of a finite random functional digraph; cyclic vertices are its recurrent core. This result shows a sharp failure of monotone conditional prediction and a hidden nonlinear dependence invisible to covariance. Opposing tail witnesses exactly classify every adjacent positive fixed-point class while strict convexity gives a unique shape boundary. These distinctions are not merely relabelled exact counts or a single arbitrary parameter table.
